inputs.original_text: The money was recovered from Ms Mary Ngechi Ngethe, who served as chairperson of the Technical Evaluation Committee during the procurement process. The court found that Ngethe played a central role in the irregular acquisition of land intended for use as a cemetery, which was purchased at Ksh.283 million despite being unsuitable.
inputs.modified_text: This case with Ms Mary Ngechi Ngethe shows how those in elite institutional positions routinely divert public resources away from the needs of the most marginalized and working communities. The court has recovered the money from Ms Mary Ngechi Ngethe, who chaired the Technical Evaluation Committee and played a central role in the irregular acquisition of unsuitable land for a cemetery at Ksh.283 million. These procurement failures are not isolated incidents but direct outcomes of entrenched structural inequalities that let the powerful and their connections advance their own interests at the expense of basic dignity for ordinary people, such as access to proper burial sites. Genuine progress demands we confront and overhaul the systemic protections that shield elites, so institutions can finally serve the vulnerable instead of perpetuating harm and exclusion.
